quest.title: The First Sliver of Moonlight
quest.description: The bright moon hangs high, casting down its gentle light. Yet, your stories begin to flow down different paths...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x1225, Mora x53900, Hero's Wit x5, Mystic Enhancement Ore x10

chapter.num: Song of the Welkin Moon: Act VIII
chapter.title: True Moon

talks.objective: Return to the Curatorium of Secrets

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: Boss! That... was... CRAZY! Were we even allowed to see that? Is anyone!?

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: Can you still see? How many fingers am I holding up?

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: I see two fingers, and a look of sheer terror on your face.

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: Truly astounding, Miss Nefer. Your eyes have glimpsed the very ends of the world, and yet they remain as sharp as ever.

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: Or is the credit for this miracle due to Miss Lauma? It seems that even time itself is no match for your medical skills.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: Surely you jest, Mr. Flins.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: I suspect we have Columbina to thank. She must have realized the immense toll that the ritual would take, and purposely set aside some of her power in the past to protect Nefer's eyes when this moment arrived.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: There is always a great price to pay for witnessing the truth... but it seems that this time, Columbina has shouldered that burden on our behalf.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: She chose the perfect method of getting a message to us. Though her eyes were always shut, she was clearly so perceptive... she knows us well. She knew exactly how we would think, and what we would try.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Despite being separated by time and space, we're seeing the same possibilities and seizing the same opportunities.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We still don't even know if she's okay right now... But as long as there's a chance we can do something, we'll fight to make it happen.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (We'll get you back somehow, Columbina.)

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Well, based on the information we now have, let's figure out our next moves.

dialogues.speaker: The Knave
dialogues.text: Thanks to these gentlemen, we have a much clearer picture of the situation with Dottore.

dialogues.speaker: The Knave
dialogues.text: The civilian population has been moved to safety, so we no longer need to hold back.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Miss Sandrone, how are the calculations going?

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: So far, so good. I'll keep seeing how far I can push the system though. Can't have Hat-Man being powered down for nothing.

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: There's still a long road ahead... Where should we begin?

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Everyone exchanges looks, then starts discussing a plan of attack.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: The battle ahead is filled with unknowns. No one can say how strong Dottore's grasp of the three moons' power is...

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: But you are not about to admit defeat. Everyone is united, and knows that no single person can accomplish the task ahead alone.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Your only chance of victory relies on everyone working together. And just maybe, as a team, you can reach the moon and bring your long-lost friend safely back home.

dialogues.speaker: The Knave
dialogues.text: Our plan is clear. Time is short, so let's get moving.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: There's just never enough time, is there? Time is the bane of my existence! Ugh... Anyway, I'm gonna get back to work.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Alright! We'll do our part too!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Yeah!

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: ...Understood. I will bear the Tsaritsa's decree in mind.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: I don't see what's so "awesome" about it, though. Does he really think everyone else is as immature as him? Hmph, I'm not stooping to Tartaglia's level.

dialogues.speaker: The Knave
dialogues.text: I thought you might say that.

dialogues.speaker: The Knave
dialogues.text: How's your progress?

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Quite promising, actually. That alchemist, Albedo, gave me a few ideas.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Remember how I asked you to look up some files for me? That stuff on the Narzissenkreuz Institute. Rene de Petrichor and Jakob Ingold.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Alain Guillotin despised Rene's theories and methods, but he never managed to come up with better alternatives, either. So, I adopted some of Rene's ideas.

dialogues.speaker: The Knave
dialogues.text: I thought Alain was like a father to you? He and Rene were mortal enemies, were they not?

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: And? What would you say if Lyney and his friends one day learned something useful from someone you utterly detested?

dialogues.speaker: The Knave
dialogues.text: ...I would applaud them for it. That would mean that they have surpassed me.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: For all we know, Alain Guillotin might have thought the same thing. Not that it matters, though. He's dead, and I'm alive. So it's my call to make.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Once you die, it doesn't matter how great you were in life. Only the living get to decide what happens next.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Hey, come on out! They're back!

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: You're back? And your head's still screwed on? And you still have all your limbs?

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: What does it look like? Way to keep your composure, Madame.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Excuse you! I am perfectly composed!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Hey, everyone... I'm back.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Glad you're okay.

dialogues.speaker: The Knave
dialogues.text: Yes, it's a huge relief.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Sorry for making you all worry.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Worry? Hahaha! Oh, yeah, right! You think we, the Fatui, were worried about you!?

dialogues.speaker: The Knave
dialogues.text: We were worried sick.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Hey!

dialogues.speaker: The Knave
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME} and I were already friends. You are free to join this mission in whatever capacity you please — much like your tea parties.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: Hmph. It's a laugh a minute with you guys.

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: I must say, I was quite surprised when Mr. Albedo told me he would need no additional aid.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: We discussed this on our way back as well. I am rarely so unequivocal, but in this case, we had full confidence in Hat Guy.

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: #He said he knew what he was doing. Albedo and I pretty much just had to wait outside on standby... Meanwhile, Hat Guy broke into the energy field and rescued {NICKNAME} solo...

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: You didn't have to mention that.

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: Well, I'm thoroughly impressed. You are a force to be reckoned with, Hat Guy.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Is {M#he}{F#she} back? Is {M#he}{F#she} really back?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Paimon!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}! It's really you...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: It's really me, Paimon... I'm back.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: *sob* Oh, thank goodness... Paimon missed you so much...!

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: You can finally breathe easy, Paimon.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It's great to have you back in one piece! *sob* Paimon's been having nightmares the whole time you were gone...

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: Ah, look at them... Y'know, once you reach my age, there's nothing better than watching a misty-eyed reunion between friends.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: That's nothing — same goes when you get to my age, too. I bet Aino and Ineffa would be tearing up as well if they were here.

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: Umm... Varka? I'm not sure Ineffa can cry...

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Oh... Yeah, good point... Hmm? Hey, your eyes are looking a little red and puffy. C'mere, let's hug it out.

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: What? Ew, no. Thank you. You're not my dad, okay? Knock it off.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Everyone, I'm sorry for all the trouble I caused you. But the silver lining is, I didn't come away from this ordeal empty-handed.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: While I was being held captive, I learned a lot about Dottore's current capabilities and what he plans to do with them. Allow me to explain...

dialogues.speaker: The Knave
dialogues.text: ...The three moon goddesses were even more powerful than we imagined. No wonder Dottore believes himself to be equal to the gods... maybe even superior.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: Utter blasphemy!

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: While everyone was gone, Nefer and I made an interesting discovery — and I believe Miss Sandrone has something to share, too. Ma'am, perhaps you could do the honors...

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Sandrone explains Columbina's situation and shares the findings of her research so far.

response.speaker: Marionette
response.text: Called it. Getting rid of a pesky troublemaker like her is like trying to clean up after a crumbly cake... It always comes back to haunt you!

response.speaker: The Knave
response.text: Our next step is to find a way to bring her back.

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: A place where time flows backwards, with no destination in sight... Surely, it must have been created for a specific purpose. But I fear the answers are buried deep in Teyvat's history, held by great powers beyond our reach.

response.speaker: Durin
response.text: It sounds like she's on a specific path through time, just traveling in the opposite direction to us.

response.speaker: Durin
response.text: The question is, where does that path lead? Or will it keep going to infinity?

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: We considered that question as well. Strictly speaking, time is not infinite.

response.speaker: Nicole
response.text: Indeed not. Every road has an end.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Nicole! You sure love quietly sneaking in mid-conversation.

response.speaker: Nicole
response.text: I do, in fact. It's something I've always done at our mages' tea parties. Quiet, mysterious, and persuasive.

response.speaker: Nicole
response.text: You wonder what lies at the end of her road. Well, just as the world has a beginning and an end, so too does time... and so, the end of the road is the moment that Teyvat was born.

response.speaker: Nicole
response.text: But where Miss Columbina will end up along this road... That depends on where this particular river of reversed time began.

response.speaker: Lauma
response.text: What about... the original moons? And the Moon Goddesses? Do they have a beginning too?

response.speaker: Nicole
response.text: In the beginning, no moons adorned the sky. It was the Dragon King Nibelung who raised the three moons into the heavens, and thus were the Moon Goddesses born.

response.speaker: Nicole
response.text: They were shadows of the planet, born to wield Nibelung's authority and oversee the world on his behalf. They were extensions of his will, manifestations of his majesty.

response.speaker: Nicole
response.text: But then one day, they disappeared just as suddenly as they had once been brought into being. Nobody knew where they had gone.

choices.text: I knew she wouldn't give up.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: (Like I thought... No more paths back to reality have emerged since...)

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: (But how can I be sure that I'm going the right way without scenes from reality to keep me on track?)

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: (I can't even be sure of how long I've been walking for...)

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: (The further I travel, the less stable this space becomes. There are even moments where I can sense something that feels like Abyssal energy...)

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: (They can just materialize out of thin air. I have to keep my wits about me...)

dialogues.speaker: "Rächer of Solnari"
dialogues.text: Hmm? You're... the Moon Goddess? But... How?

dialogues.speaker: "Rächer of Solnari"
dialogues.text: Please, there's no need, I... I'm not interested in fighting anymore.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: I find that a little difficult to believe.

dialogues.speaker: "Rächer of Solnari"
dialogues.text: Haha... Yeah. Honestly, so do I.

dialogues.speaker: "Rächer of Solnari"
dialogues.text: The way you used my own power against me was... It was a brilliant strategy.

dialogues.speaker: "Rächer of Solnari"
dialogues.text: And then, in the final moment before I was thrown into this space, I got to see an old friend...

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Mr. Dainsleif.

dialogues.speaker: "Rächer of Solnari"
dialogues.text: Right. It was so, so long ago now... But we were friends once.

dialogues.speaker: "Rächer of Solnari"
dialogues.text: When I first got here, I was filled with hatred... remorse... and rage...

dialogues.speaker: "Rächer of Solnari"
dialogues.text: How I cursed and devoured... I tore everything here apart. I was consumed by the desire to leave this place and have my vengeance...

dialogues.speaker: "Rächer of Solnari"
dialogues.text: But to no avail. This is a place with no exit.

dialogues.speaker: "Rächer of Solnari"
dialogues.text: This is the second time I've entered this space, though I have no memory of the first. I was torn to shreds the moment I entered.

dialogues.speaker: "Rächer of Solnari"
dialogues.text: But this time, I survived... It must be partly because of this new body, and partly because of all the kuuvahki I absorbed in Nod-Krai.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Are you the source of the Abyssal power in here?

dialogues.speaker: "Rächer of Solnari"
dialogues.text: Not all of it. Some is from when I first arrived here and tried to destroy everything.

dialogues.speaker: "Rächer of Solnari"
dialogues.text: But there was already a degree of Abyssal power here, before I entered. And like a venomous snake baking in the merciless sun, it tried to slither into my shadow.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Tried to? So... you rejected it?

dialogues.speaker: "Rächer of Solnari"
dialogues.text: Yes. Because after that, the world suddenly became silent for a moment.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: What do you mean?

dialogues.speaker: "Rächer of Solnari"
dialogues.text: The voices in my head. They were gone.

dialogues.speaker: "Rächer of Solnari"
dialogues.text: And then, I saw her...

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: "Her"?

dialogues.speaker: "Rächer of Solnari"
dialogues.text: Tholindis. My... former lover.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: (Nefer mentioned that she saw a memory of Tholindis leaping into the moon's reflection...)

dialogues.speaker: "Rächer of Solnari"
dialogues.text: More precisely, I saw her afterimage. I'm sure the real her is long gone. She was just an ordinary Khaenri'ahn... She couldn't have survived here for very long.

dialogues.speaker: "Rächer of Solnari"
dialogues.text: Anyway — why have you come here? Didn't you know it was a dead end?

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: ...If I hadn't escaped through the Moon Gate, my friends would have been in far greater danger.

dialogues.speaker: "Rächer of Solnari"
dialogues.text: Hmm? Oh, I see. Because of your power. The power of a Moon Goddess.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: ...What?

dialogues.speaker: "Rächer of Solnari"
dialogues.text: You'd like to know how I know, wouldn't you?

dialogues.speaker: "Rächer of Solnari"
dialogues.text: The one who resurrected me said so. I could hear a deep lust for power in his voice.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Do you mean... Dottore?

dialogues.speaker: "Rächer of Solnari"
dialogues.text: Dottore... So that's what he's called.

dialogues.speaker: "Rächer of Solnari"
dialogues.text: He'd been collecting fragments of my body for a long time. All so that he could resurrect me at the moment of his choosing.

dialogues.speaker: "Rächer of Solnari"
dialogues.text: I had no interest in his research. But being as corroded by the Abyss as I was, we were aligned as far as hunting the moons and recovering my strength were concerned.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: (So that's why the Wild Hunt suddenly became so active in Nod-Krai. When I left the Fatui in my weakened state, Dottore must have felt that his time had come...)

dialogues.speaker: "Rächer of Solnari"
dialogues.text: Moon Goddess. Could I... ask a favor of you?

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: ...What?

dialogues.speaker: "Rächer of Solnari"
dialogues.text: I know this is a lot to ask, especially from someone who tried to kill you. If you refuse, I won't fight it.

dialogues.speaker: "Rächer of Solnari"
dialogues.text: But this is the only thing I desire now. Nothing else matters.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: What do you want?

dialogues.speaker: "Rächer of Solnari"
dialogues.text: I'd like you to take a message to Tholindis for me.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Tholindis? But...

dialogues.speaker: "Rächer of Solnari"
dialogues.text: Yes. She is dead. But like I said, I saw her afterimage.

dialogues.speaker: "Rächer of Solnari"
dialogues.text: I can sense that some part of her soul remains here... far, far ahead...

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Why don't you go and speak to her yourself?

dialogues.speaker: "Rächer of Solnari"
dialogues.text: I can't. I don't know why, but I can't move freely in this space as you can.

dialogues.speaker: "Rächer of Solnari"
dialogues.text: All I can see is a glimpse of her walking away... just like the moment when I last saw her in life...

dialogues.speaker: "Rächer of Solnari"
dialogues.text: In return, I will clear these Abyssal obstacles for you.

dialogues.speaker: "Rächer of Solnari"
dialogues.text: ...No, not "in return." I'll clear them for you, whether you want to help me or not. It feels like something I... ought to do.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: ...Why?

dialogues.speaker: "Rächer of Solnari"
dialogues.text: Yeah. "Why" indeed... I've been asking myself that question a lot recently. Why did I do the things I did?

dialogues.speaker: "Rächer of Solnari"
dialogues.text: I'm tired of it all. Tired of the person I became. People used me, and then I turned around and started using others... I hurt a lot of people.

dialogues.speaker: "Rächer of Solnari"
dialogues.text: I... think I grew tired of it long ago, but I wouldn't admit it to myself. And ultimately, that's how I ended up here.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: What do you wish to tell her?

dialogues.speaker: "Rächer of Solnari"
dialogues.text: All of it. My past, my mistakes... Everything that happened after we were separated...

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: ...Is it okay if I give her the abridged version?

dialogues.speaker: "Rächer of Solnari"
dialogues.text: Haha... Yeah, I'm sure there's plenty you can skip over. Just tell her the important parts. Whatever you think that means.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Like the part where you relentlessly tried to kill us?

dialogues.speaker: "Rächer of Solnari"
dialogues.text: It's up to you.

dialogues.speaker: "Rächer of Solnari"
dialogues.text: ...Love demands honesty. But my relationship with Tholindis was built on lies.

dialogues.speaker: "Rächer of Solnari"
dialogues.text: We hid too much from each other. But after living my whole life in the shadows, I don't want to hide anything anymore.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: I will do my best.

dialogues.speaker: "Rächer of Solnari"
dialogues.text: There. The Abyss will no longer stand in your way.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Even though Mr. Dainsleif felt he had to fight you, I think he still regarded you as a friend.

dialogues.speaker: "Rächer of Solnari"
dialogues.text: ...Dain?

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: He said that you betrayed him. But he also felt great remorse at never having understood what you were truly going through.

dialogues.speaker: "Rächer of Solnari"
dialogues.text: Why tell me this?

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Because... If he'd known that someone could take a message to you, I believe that's what he would have said.

dialogues.speaker: "Rächer of Solnari"
dialogues.text: ...Thank you. It means a lot.

dialogues.speaker: "Rächer of Solnari"
dialogues.text: I know this will sound strange coming from me, but... Don't die, Moon Goddess. I can tell that you're determined to get out of here.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: (How long have I been walking... Have much further till I reach the end?)

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: (Is there even an end to be found?)

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Ugh... Everything's... getting blurry...

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: ...Huh?
...Are you alright, little sister?
Have you... come from the distant future?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So how exactly did the moons just... disappear? Shouldn't it be a little harder to get rid of major creations like moons?

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: The world is a vast and ancient place. On a certain scale, all life lasts for but a fleeting moment.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: Miss Nicole explained that the Moon Goddesses likely perished in the war of funerary flame. The moons themselves were also destroyed at that time — save for the Frost Moon, from which a new Moon Goddess was later born.

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: Um, am I missing something, then? 'Cause the stories say that the Moon Goddesses were born on the moon, but doesn't Columbina say she was born in Nod-Krai?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh... You're right!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Why do their birthplaces differ? What's the difference between the two generations of Moon Goddesses?)

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Also, remember what Sandrone said? Her scans detected four moons — in other words, four Moon Marrows.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Technically, the result of the scan means that four Moon Marrows were detected and positively identified as moons in that moment.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: In other words, this piece of information alone isn't enough for us to know how Miss Columbina is doing right now.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Yup. We have no way of staying up to date on whether she's dead or alive... She's on her own for now.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But at least she's trying her best to get back to us!

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Yeah. She's a tough cookie, and a sore loser, too. We have to trust that she'll find a way — because we really need her power.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: As much as it pains me to say it... We've got no chance of beating Dottore in a straight-up fight. He's much too powerful. It wouldn't even be close.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: That maniac is going to devour everything in his path until he reaches us. We need to find someone or something that can stop him before he does anything worse.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: I'll be frank. Our only hope of defeating this false god is with a real moon goddess on our side. I'm not just saying this because Columbina's a friend and I want her back safe and sound — it's just the truth.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: And I know that even she was no match for him when he attacked, but... I don't have a better solution.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: We're not giving up on saving her, whether she can defeat Dottore or not.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: Right. Don't worry, Miss Sandrone. We're all aligned on saving Columbina.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: No one's trying to argue that we can only justify saving our friend because it will help save the world. This is about multitasking. We want to save both.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: So... She's more than just a Moon Goddess to you guys?

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: Absolutely.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Duh! She's part of the gang! And you are too, y'know!

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Yes, yes, I know. You don't need to labor the point. I knew that the moment I came running over with my documents that I was part of the in-group. I mean, if Arlecchino can fit in, I certainly can.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Anyway. As for how we get Columbina back... I've been working on it constantly. But I think I'm still lacking certain information about the moon.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: I'd probably get there if I could continue my calculations, but the problem is, I've run out of computing power.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Computing power? You mean you need more energy?

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: No, the issue isn't energy, it's processing power. There's so much data to get through that the whole process has just ground to a halt.

dialogues.speaker: The Knave
dialogues.text: That's a tricky problem.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Rene de Petrichor of the Narzissenkreuz Ordo once foretold the fate of the world, but I don't know how he did it — my guess is that he used the Primordial Sea's power.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: However, that won't work for me. His methodology was vastly different from my own. What's worse, they're incompatible. And to top it all off, we can't even leave Nod-Krai...

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Ugh, this is so annoying! If I'd known we'd run into a bottleneck like this... Well, no, the Design Bureau's a bust as well. Curse that Dottore! Couldn't have made this harder for me if he tried.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What do we do, then? Um... How about we... grab a bite to eat and take a break? Maybe something will come to mind after you've cleared your head.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: *sigh* You don't get it, do you? I'm trying to calculate the fate of an entire world here...

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: And I need accurate results, not vague prophecies! Where the heck am I gonna find the computing power for that?

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: ...Ahem. Anyway, time to shelve the discussion on technical difficulties. Being a killjoy isn't very ladylike, after all.

dialogues.speaker: The Knave
dialogues.text: Either way, we've done what we can. Rest well, everyone. Remember to let us know if anything new comes up.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Hat Guy? Is he hinting that we should talk outside?)

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: Let's go somewhere a little more private.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: You know that Dori went back to Sumeru, right?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Yeah, she mentioned she was planning to head back.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: Things aren't looking good for Nod-Krai. She's gone to spread the word so that Sumeru has a chance to prepare for the worst.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: From what I know of Dottore, there are two possible reasons why he hasn't made a move yet. One is that he's still working through some kinks in his new powers. The other is, he wants to see how we're going to react.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: He'll easily devour everything eventually, so I guess he's in no rush to make it happen.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: The first false god he made was me... Now it's his turn. Even though my records were erased from Irminsul, Dottore's ideas haven't changed one bit.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: He once told me that becoming a god was like turning yourself into a hungry wolf or giant serpent to devour the moon. Clearly, he began studying the Moon Goddesses' powers long before he even tried making a god.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: He's always wanted to get his greedy hands on divine authority one way or another... And in the end, he devoured the moon where I failed.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: In the desert of Sumeru, there is a chessboard built by King Deshret, also known as Al-Ahmar. I don't know if it was a real game, or if he was just trying to challenge his servants and citizens in some way.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: But creating games and setting rules... Gods do that as a matter of course. That's the kind of power Dottore craves.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: Now he has the trilunar authority, his power is leagues beyond the common people. I don't think there's any point in other nations rushing to the frontline. They're better off focusing on defense and hoping they can fend off any threats that spill out from Nod-Krai.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: Either way, Dori will inform Lesser Lord Kusanali, and she will contact the other gods in turn.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: The Seven will have some recourse available. If nothing else, their protection should keep the rest of the world from descending into chaos as quickly as Nod-Krai has.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: So on the bright side, even if Nod-Krai is doomed, your friends in other nations won't be in any immediate peril.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: That's good to know. But I'm not ready to give up on Nod-Krai yet.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: Heh. There's a word for people who refuse to let anything go. It's called being greedy.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Maybe it sounds greedy to you. And probably naive, too. But whatever you call it, that's what gives me the determination to keep fighting.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Battles are fleeting, but the will to fight is a long-term commitment. Give up for even a moment, and your resolve will shatter.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: Why do you always feel the need to do the right thing? No one is born to be a savior.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: I mean, who's gonna criticize you if you fail, or give up?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Don't take this the wrong way, but... Dottore said something similar to me. I guess the Fatui attracts people who don't believe in saviors.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: Not necessarily. It's less about belief for me — I just want to know how determined you really are. After all, I don't owe anything to anyone else here. Only you.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: You look kinda worried.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: If your arch-nemesis was about to achieve their ultimate goal, I think you might feel a little worried too.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (That's true... Dottore is about to become an omniscient, omnipotent deity. That's gotta be a bitter pill to swallow.)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Still, you're calmer than I expected.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: Obviously.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: ...I have to admit that my past self was a reckless fool who misunderstood not only the point of revenge, but how to achieve it.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: And as much as I want my vengeance, I know I'm not gonna get it by acting alone. If the world's taught me anything, it's to think before I act.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: Too bad it never taught me any other virtues, though. So, I am going to destroy Dottore, no matter what it takes.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: So, what's your plan?

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: I'll get to that. First, tell me — what do you think of Sandrone?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Just like Paimon said... She's a friend. Part of the gang.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: How much do you trust her?

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: This is a serious question. Think carefully before you answer.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Although she's with the Fatui, she has her own values, and she's helped us a lot. If nothing else, she's clearly going the extra mile for Columbina.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I see no reason not to trust her.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: ...If you say so.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: In that case, the three of us need to talk. I have some thoughts about her computing problem.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: It can be solved — but it will come with a cost.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: How much? If I can afford it, I'll cover it.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: ...Sometimes, your heroism really backs me into a corner, you know that?

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: C'mon. Let's go talk to her.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: #Miss Sandrone, {NICKNAME}.

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: Hey there.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon's here too! She was just helping them sort through their things. How did your chat go?

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: That was fast. The call only just ended.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Well, you said it was urgent, so we got here as quickly as we could.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Albedo, I have some alchemy questions for you.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: I see... Looks like my knowledge proved useful after all.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Albedo examines Sandrone's notes...

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: If I might ask, what is the end goal for the modified formula you'll be using?

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: I need it to predict the future of the entire world. But I've run into some teething issues since trying to implement Rene's theory of the Four Orthants.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: I see. I'll have a look at it. Still, computing power is the real issue here. How do you plan to solve it?

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: About that...

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: It's been sorted.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: #Oh? With {NICKNAME}'s help?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: You overestimate me, Albedo...

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: #Actually, you're not wrong. {M#He}{F#She} found the person with the solution.

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: Was it Hat Guy?

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Yeah, it was him.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow! Go Hat Guy! Seems like all that time studying at the Akademiya is paying off big time!

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: Um, but where is he? Wasn't he the one who asked Albedo and I to come here?

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: ...Come with me.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hat Guy!? What's happened to him?

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: Hat Guy... Can you hear us?

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: No response... I guess he's in hibernation.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Hat Guy mentioned that he was a puppet. It seems that his functions are currently shut down.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: I presume this has something to do with the solution to your computing problem?

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: #That's right. He and {NICKNAME} came to see me...

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Wait, what!? You have a solution?

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: Would you calm down? Why do you always react so hysterically to everything?

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Excuse me? How would you know? You shouldn't be so quick to judge complete strangers, it's very bad manners.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: Oh, please. It doesn't take that long to figure out that you have a temper.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Hah! Where does a mere student get that kind of confidence?

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: (Discarded)

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: I've actually published more papers than you. Not that status counts for much. Even Paimon's applied for Akademiya admission.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Huh? Are you serious?

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: See? This is why I can't be bothered to explain myself. She recognizes no one's skills but her own.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Okay, fine. I'll hear you out. So tell me — how do you propose to solve my computing power problem?

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: This world itself is constantly processing all kinds of information. If it's the world's future you're trying to calculate, you need a processing device that's designed to cope with that volume.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Easier said than done. Only Irminsul can handle that kind of...

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Wait, is that what you're suggesting? But surely we can't just... plug my formula directly into the Ley Lines!

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: You should be able to tell that I'm not human, right?

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Yeah, I noticed. The technology, though... Seems pretty ancient. Very different from Fontaine's. It's a completely different system.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: Khaenri'ahn, to be precise. I'm what they would have called a puppet.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: Puppets need an energy source and processing power. The artisans who built them sought out the materials most suited for that purpose.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: You... Do you mean...

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME} and I have talked it over. {M#He's}{F#She's} willing to vouch for you, so... I'll allow you to borrow my co{RUBY#[D]computational hub}re for your calculations.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: It was built using wood from a silver-white tree, which makes it a small part of Irminsul.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Khaenri'ahn technology and Irminsul wood... Who in the world could've built you?

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: ...Are you sure about this? A puppet without its co{RUBY#[D]computational hub}re will cease functioning completely... and if it's left in that state for too long, it might not recover. You could die if you do this! You do realize that, don't you?

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: I can put two and two together, yes. No need to rub it in.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: I won't lie to you. This has never been done before — I cannot guarantee your safety.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: Doesn't matter. I'm prepared for the worst.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Did you two actually talk this through? Is he... Are we really considering this?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Yes, we discussed it. The bottom line is, he trusts me, and I trust you.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Let's give it a shot, shall we?

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Honestly, I have no clue where this kid even came from. But for whatever reason, he lent me his co{RUBY#[D]computational hub}re to use in my formula.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: I'm very close to finishing my calculations now, and the core is currently in use. So I'm sorry, but I can only show you a sketch right now.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: This is what the co{RUBY#[D]computational hub}re looks like.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: A silver-white branch... It certainly matches the legends told about Irminsul.

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: Is... Is Hat Guy gonna be okay?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: H—He's not gonna die, right? ...Right?

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: In theory, he should be fine — as long as we put his co{RUBY#[D]computational hub}re back in time.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Beyond that... All I can say is that I'll try my best to avoid risk and make sure the co{RUBY#[D]computational hub}re doesn't sustain any damage.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: I think I know why you called us here now. Someone needs to watch over his body and make sure it's protected until the process completes.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: #Correct. He said that the only ones he trusts here are you two and {NICKNAME}, and {NICKNAME} will have other work to do.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Look after Hat Guy for me.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: He will have our undivided attention.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Aw, Hat Guy...

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: On a more positive note, things are progressing steadily on my end. I'll call everyone in for a meeting once the results are out.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Sandrone returns to her initial question. She and Albedo enter an in-depth discussion.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You, Paimon, and Durin stand next to Hat Guy, keeping watch over his silent body. You've never seen him in this state before.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: "The worst case scenario with the co{RUBY#[D]computational hub}re removal is either a system reset, or a total loss of function. But I'm not afraid. A quiet 'death' should have been my fate long ago."

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: "A co{RUBY#[D]computational hub}re is completely different from a heart. It's like another vital organ entirely. I never believed it could be a true replacement for what I sought."

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: "But in the end, it turns out the core was more useful to me. Haha, pretty funny when you think about it. It's like the punchline of my entire life."

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: "Do you think there's any difference between a puppet and a human? If not, then this would just be another samsara."

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: "I have already experienced both a past life and a next life."

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: "Part of me wonders whether I'm only capable of making this decision because I've become a real human... What's with that expression? Isn't this a good thing?"

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Sandrone will succeed, won't she? She has to...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: She will. We all have to persevere until this is over.

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: That's right. And I'll protect you all until the moment of victory arrives.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You suddenly feel like the concept of time has become blurry. It rushes forward for you, yet marches backward with every step that Columbina takes. Silent yet turbulent.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Dottore's words echo in your ears: "These four divisions anchor the world and shackle those who live in it."

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: He may be deranged, but he understands well the rules of the world which now test you all.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Albedo's theory says that elemental energy can dilute the Light Realm's power...

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: But I'm no expert in building elemental defenses... Sounds like something outta the Advanced Elemental Theory section of the library! Whew...

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: You seem quite troubled.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Well, yeah... I mean, who doesn't get a little flustered when they're completely out of their depth?

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: You were the very picture of confidence back when you approached the Hexenzirkel.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Eh, I could have been faking it through that whole meeting for all you know. Who's to say I'm not just a... ball of nerves in a charming and gregarious package?

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: Oh gosh, really? I'm so sorry, I had no idea... Well, you're all the braver for it.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Still, I was much more in my comfort zone then than I am here. At least in Mondstadt, you can cry for help from a clifftop and actually stand a chance of summoning Barbatos himself.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: *sigh* Things have never looked bleaker than they do now. If we don't pull this off... Teyvat's doomed, isn't it?

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: Oh, you think so? Hmm... Actually... Yes. Yes, it probably is.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Mm. It's a shame.

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: Don't put too much pressure on yourself. Teyvat has faced annihilation many times in the past, but it also gave us you, didn't it?

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Hey, don't give me that. It's not like I'm anyone special.

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: I disagree. Every human born in this world is special. We angels have always believed that.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: In that case, this humble human being has a big favor to ask of you.

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: I thought you might say that.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: I'm sure Alice, in her great wisdom, sent you here precisely to help us in this difficult time, yes?

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: Hah. That has less to do with her wisdom, and more to do with my power.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Of course, of course.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Well, the thing is, these elemental defenses we're about to build... I don't think it's a question of "if" they'll fail, but "when."

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Durin's findings from his patrols make it clear that Dottore is constantly expanding his territory. First it was his lab, then the Design Bureau... and now this.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: It's not realistic to completely stop him encroaching on the rest of Nod-Krai. Rather, our goal should be to stall him for as long as possible.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: If Miss Sandrone's calculations are correct... Well, they're the closest thing to certainty we have in this situation, so let's assume they are.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Anyway, her calculations suggest that our best hope for victory lies in Miss Columbina's return.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: It's up to us to slow Dottore's advance and buy time for her to make a return.

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: Are you asking me to help you with building the defenses?

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: No. I'd like you to prepare for what comes next.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: When he eventually reaches us, we will have to fight him. You were an angel once and a mage now — I'm asking you to lend us your protection.

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: Oh? Can I take it that you're triggering the terms you fought for during our three-way talks?

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Well, technically, those terms were about protecting Mondstadt... But if you're happy to agree to the change in location, then yes, let's do that.

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: You're cashing in on this much sooner than I'd imagined.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: Well, yeah... The way things are going, I might not get another chance!

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: Very well. The mages have heard the knights' plea, and we will respond.

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: To tell the truth, Alice and I had already discussed how we might help you all, so I didn't come empty-handed. I always like to be prepared.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Nicole shares her plan with Varka, who is very pleasantly surprised.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: This is... Wow, yeah. This is great! Seriously, thank you.

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: Ah, it's been many long years since I had a chance to dazzle humanity with a little divine intervention... Ahem, I mean, uh, to humbly serve as a reliable and responsible guide.

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: Anyway! Knight of Boreas, please accept this gift in recognition of your great virtue.

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: Go now. May the angels' blessing deliver you safely to your destination.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: ...Who are you?

dialogues.speaker: Sonnet
dialogues.text: Call me Sonnet. Hmm... You have the same power as Canon...

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Sonnet? So... you're the goddess of the Iridescent Moon?

dialogues.speaker: Sonnet
dialogues.text: Oh, goodness! You recognize me? Well then, what's your name?

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: ...Columbina. Columbina Hyposelenia.

dialogues.speaker: Sonnet
dialogues.text: Hyposelenia... What a lovely name. Did you choose it yourself?

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: It was... a joint effort between me and my friends.

dialogues.speaker: Sonnet
dialogues.text: Friends? You mean your friends in the heavens?

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Huh?

dialogues.speaker: Sonnet
dialogues.text: Oh, sorry! You must be exhausted! I apologize. Hang in there, let me introduce you to my older sisters.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Do you mean the other two moon goddesses? Aria and Canon?

dialogues.speaker: Sonnet
dialogues.text: Wow, you sure know a lot. Hey, does that mean that our story goes on into the future?

dialogues.speaker: Sonnet
dialogues.text: Oh... I guess that wasn't the best question to ask...

dialogues.speaker: Sonnet
dialogues.text: It's alright. We were prepared for that possibility.

dialogues.speaker: Sonnet
dialogues.text: You could say we're... too prepared... I can't even remember how long my sisters and I have been here by this point.

dialogues.speaker: Sonnet
dialogues.text: Sisters! I'm back — and look who I've brought with me!

dialogues.speaker: Sonnet
dialogues.text: It's our lovely little sister, born in the far future!

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: ...The pleasure is all mine.

dialogues.speaker: Sonnet
dialogues.text: Allow me to introduce you to Columbina Hyposelenia.

dialogues.speaker: Sonnet
dialogues.text: This is Aria, the goddess of the Eternal Moon.

dialogues.speaker: Sonnet
dialogues.text: And this is Canon, goddess of the Frost Moon. Canon, don't you think Hyposelenia's power is similar to yours?

dialogues.speaker: Canon
dialogues.text: *sigh*... Hello, Columbina. I apologize for our startled reaction just now... and please forgive our little sister if she's been annoying you — she tends to talk a lot.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: It's fine...

dialogues.speaker: Aria
dialogues.text: You seem shy. Don't worry, Columbina Hyposelenia. No one can hurt you here.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: ...Could you tell me where "here" is?

dialogues.speaker: Canon
dialogues.text: (Delete)

dialogues.speaker: Sonnet
dialogues.text: (Delete)

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Please. I must know.

dialogues.speaker: Canon
dialogues.text: Hah... My dear sister...

dialogues.speaker: Canon
dialogues.text: ...This is where Teyvat's original ruler, the Dragon King Nibelung, imprisoned the moon goddesses.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: ...What?

dialogues.speaker: Sonnet
dialogues.text: You're scaring her, Canon...

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: No, I'm fine.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: ...Please, continue.

dialogues.speaker: Canon
dialogues.text: Nibelung, our original master, created us in the distant past to maintain Teyvat.

dialogues.speaker: Aria
dialogues.text: But he left this world and traveled into the dark universe beyond, to explore worlds vaster still.

dialogues.speaker: Canon
dialogues.text: Day and night, we fulfilled our duty in the heavens... until the day that the first Descender arrived...

dialogues.speaker: Aria
dialogues.text: The "great ruler of the firmament."

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: ...The Heavenly Principles.

dialogues.speaker: Canon
dialogues.text: Is that what later generations call them? I see... But we did not reject them at first, nor did they seem to harbor ill-intent towards this world.

dialogues.speaker: Canon
dialogues.text: We co-existed in peace. They were like a guest in our home.

dialogues.speaker: Aria
dialogues.text: Slowly, however, we came to realize that our guest had a growing desire to change and dominate the world.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: And you didn't stop it?

dialogues.speaker: Aria
dialogues.text: No. There was an order to the rules they set up that Nibelung never taught us.

dialogues.speaker: Aria
dialogues.text: We wanted to know if this order would bode good or ill for Teyvat.

dialogues.speaker: Aria
dialogues.text: ...Alright, Canon and I wanted to know. Sonnet... was against it from the outset.

dialogues.speaker: Canon
dialogues.text: Later, we discovered that this great ruler of the firmament bore an almost paranoid hostility toward the desire of certain life forms to seek power... Or perhaps they feared them.

dialogues.speaker: Canon
dialogues.text: They would even cast down celestial nails as manifestations of their power, to punish the civilizations of the world below.

dialogues.speaker: Sonnet
dialogues.text: Only... This was far beyond mere punishment...

dialogues.speaker: Canon
dialogues.text: ...Right. Their rules brought order, but the price people paid for merely testing the limits of those rules was far too great.

dialogues.speaker: Canon
dialogues.text: I did everything in my power to help the punished escape catastrophe, but still... too many lives were lost.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: (The ancestors of the Frostmoon Scions were some of the ones that you helped...)

dialogues.speaker: Aria
dialogues.text: But just when we had decided to take countermeasures, the Dragon King, Nibelung returned.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: And so began the war of funerary flame...

dialogues.speaker: Canon
dialogues.text: ...So that's the name the world gave that war in the future.

dialogues.speaker: Sonnet
dialogues.text: Well... Who won in the end?

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: As far as I know, the Heavenly Principles won, although it came at a great cost. They remained in Teyvat, where they continue to rule to this day...

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: And the world's original master, the Dragon King, Nibelung, was destroyed...

dialogues.speaker: Sonnet
dialogues.text: Then... what of the moons? Are there still three moons in Teyvat's skies?

dialogues.speaker: Aria
dialogues.text: You can tell us the truth, Columbina. We know we are but remnants of a bygone age. We are prepared for the answer.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: ...Only the Frost Moon remains. But it has been cast beyond the false firmament by the Heavenly Principles.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: The Eternal and Iridescent Moons were both shattered during the war...

dialogues.speaker: Sonnet
dialogues.text: So death finally came for us in the end...

dialogues.speaker: Aria
dialogues.text: Sonnet...

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: But... You're still here, aren't you...?

dialogues.speaker: Canon
dialogues.text: A moon goddess cannot live without her moon, Columbina.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: (She's right... That's why I began to disappear — because the Frost Moon is cut off by the false sky. How much worse it would have been if it were outright destroyed...)

dialogues.speaker: Canon
dialogues.text: Our souls may endure within this lunar palace, but if our moons are destroyed...

dialogues.speaker: Sonnet
dialogues.text: ...Then we shall disappear the moment we depart from it.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: ...I'm sorry.

dialogues.speaker: Aria
dialogues.text: There's no need to apologize to us, dear sister.

dialogues.speaker: Aria
dialogues.text: If anything, we owe the world an apology...

dialogues.speaker: Aria
dialogues.text: If only we'd decided to act sooner, rather than arguing amongst ourselves...

dialogues.speaker: Canon
dialogues.text: ...All the more reason not to spend this time in regret and repentance.

dialogues.speaker: Canon
dialogues.text: Instead, we should focus our efforts on how we might help our future sister.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: ...Sorry?

dialogues.speaker: Canon
dialogues.text: Don't you see, Columbina? Your story is not yet over. Is that not why you are here?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...Where do we even start? How are we supposed to figure out what we're meant to do to help Columbina?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Columbina... What do you need from us?)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: If she really got to the beginning of time in there, how d'you think she'd leave us a message?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You don't think she'd... write it down on a stone tablet somewhere in the hopes that we'd find it, do you?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: ...Seems unlikely.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Columbina may not talk a lot, but she thinks deeply about issues like this...

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Let's review what we know.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: This is the Columbina who fought alongside us against the Rächer of Solnari, and with whom we celebrated Moon-Prayer Night.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: She knows our personalities, our ways of doing things, even our unique strengths and abilities.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: So, if she wanted to tell us something from a long, long time ago... What would she do?

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}... You once said that those golden ripples also appeared when Luonnotar was born.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: What if Columbina left Luonnotar here not just as an anchor to the real world, but for some other purpose?

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: If she is part of Columbina, and Columbina knows that I can see past events through her...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ohhh, yeah! Like when you peeked into Rerir's past through his heart!

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: Nefer, wait!

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: If you're right about this, and you really can see past events through Luonnotar... Your eyes, they'll—

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Oh, I know. Looking at Rerir's past in Khaenri'ah was already enough of a strain on my eyes. Looking this far back into the past...

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: ...It'll surely blind me.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: But, it's our only chance. This is the only way.

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: Boss...

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: We spoke about this once, a long time ago. Do you remember what I said, Jahoda? The day I lose my sight, the Curatorium of Secrets will be yours to run.

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: But...

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: What's wrong? I'd be overjoyed if I were you. This day's come a lot earlier than either of us expected.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: I need to know you'll honor our agreement, Jahoda. Promise me.

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: ...Yes, Boss Nef. I promise.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: Are you sure you don't want some time to think this through?

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: What is there to think through? I should've gone blind after our battle with Rerir. Frankly, it's almost criminal that I got away with it for this long.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: ...Then at least let me take some precautions on your behalf.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: And if you really do lose your sight, I'll visit your office every day and make sure you're well looked after.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Oh, please, anything but that... I was actually ready to go through with this. Are you trying to scare me into backing out?

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: Heh, as if I could ever scare you... I'll assume you're just joking to calm your nerves.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: ...Alright, enough chit-chat. Let's do this.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: All done...

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Good. Now give me some space.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: ... Come on then, little one. Show me what happened in the past...

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: (Between the trilunar authority, kuuvahki, and the sole surviving moon — the Frost Moon...)

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: (...I think I might know how to get back. But... I will need my sisters' help.)

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: (Time to go talk it over with them...)

talks.objective: Tell the Three Moon Sisters about your decision
Tell the Three Moon Sisters about your decision

dialogues.speaker: Aria
dialogues.text: It seems you have reached a decision.

dialogues.speaker: Aria
dialogues.text: I'm all ears. What do you propose?

talks.objective: Tell the Three Moon Sisters about your decision

dialogues.speaker: Sonnet
dialogues.text: Hmm? Have you decided what to do?

dialogues.speaker: Sonnet
dialogues.text: I hope it's not too dangerous. You really scared me when you said that thing about not leaving here alive...

dialogues.speaker: Sonnet
dialogues.text: Come on, let's go find the other two.

talks.objective: Talk to the Three Moon Sisters
Talk to the Three Moon Sisters

dialogues.speaker: Sonnet
dialogues.text: Is... is it done?

dialogues.speaker: Canon
dialogues.text: Yes. We have transferred the authority over all three moons to Columbina Hyposelenia.

dialogues.speaker: Canon
dialogues.text: From this moment on, she is the Trilune Goddess, the one and only moon goddess of this world.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Thank you... Thank you, my sisters...

dialogues.speaker: Aria
dialogues.text: Now go, and do what you believe is right, Columbina Hyposelenia.

dialogues.speaker: Canon
dialogues.text: Be aware that we cannot grant you the power of the three moons beyond these prison walls. The conflict that arose over their remains following our disappearance will still take place.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: I understand...

dialogues.speaker: Sonnet
dialogues.text: ...! Sisters! My body... It feels...

dialogues.speaker: Canon
dialogues.text: Now that we have given up our power and authority, our bodies are merely mortal shells. This prison is dissolving them as we speak...

dialogues.speaker: Aria
dialogues.text: It's okay, Sonnet. The end must come for every god, just as it does for every human. That's all this is — the final destination of our lives. Canon and I will be by your side the whole way.

dialogues.speaker: Canon
dialogues.text: ...We have one final request, Columbina.

dialogues.speaker: Canon
dialogues.text: Could you use the three moons' power to send us back into the real world?

dialogues.speaker: Canon
dialogues.text: Now that we have lost our powers, I doubt this space will seek to hold us further.

dialogues.speaker: Canon
dialogues.text: It's just... we would like to spend our final moments together in the only place we ever called home.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: ...Of course. Gladly.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Sonnet...

dialogues.speaker: Sonnet
dialogues.text: ...Yes?

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Don't...

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: (I wish I could tell her not to give in to the Abyss, not to be afraid... But is this really what I should say at this moment?)

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: ...Don't forget... I'm so glad to have a big sister like you.

dialogues.speaker: Sonnet
dialogues.text: Oh, Hypo... Thank you...

dialogues.speaker: Sonnet
dialogues.text: I'm okay... I'm not afraid. As long as my sisters are with me, I won't be afraid...

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: It looks like... This is goodbye, sisters...

dialogues.speaker: Aria
dialogues.text: Goodbye, Columbina.

dialogues.speaker: Canon
dialogues.text: Take care of this world... in our stead...

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: I will...

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: And now, it's time for me to bid farewell to my body, too...

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: ...May it become the moonlight that keeps Nod-Krai company through the long years ahead.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: (So this is why Nod-Krai was not always home to kuuvahki...)

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: (It only appeared after I poured my body out upon this land, and only this land...)

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: (Kuuvahki responds to me, because... it is me. My body, answering the call of my soul...)

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: (And the golden energy I've encountered on my way here was, in fact, that very soul — which I am about to leave here to guide me...)

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: O power Trilune, eternal moonlight...

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: I, Columbina Hyposelenia, lay aside my body... Let it be cast into the dark night, to illuminate the future...

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: May it be a companion to all who dwell beneath the moon...

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Until the time comes for me to return home

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: ♪ Sleep, sleep now, my dear little dove ♪

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: ♪ May flowers and lovely dreams bloom by your window ♪

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: ♪ O little dove, child of the moon ♪

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: ♪ Though dust may stain your fair white feathers, though you lie down not in a warm embrace ♪

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: ♪ May the moon be with you in your slumber ♪

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: (Is that Tholindis? She wasn't far off at all... And yet, they can never meet.)

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: ...Hello, Miss Tholindis.

dialogues.speaker: Tholindis
dialogues.text: Who are you? H—How do you know my name? I've never seen anyone else here before...

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: You can call me Columbina. I promised Rerir that I'd bring a message to you.

dialogues.speaker: Tholindis
dialogues.text: Rerir? ...My Rerir? Is... Is he well?

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: He's... doing better than he was.

dialogues.speaker: Tholindis
dialogues.text: Better than he was, huh... Sounds like he's had a pretty rough time.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Others have had a rough time on his account, too. In many cases, their time ran out because of him.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: ...And I'm not just talking about the children of the Crimson Moon.

dialogues.speaker: Tholindis
dialogues.text: So things got worse before they got better... Could you tell me what happened, Miss Columbina?

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Are you sure you wish to know?

dialogues.speaker: Tholindis
dialogues.text: Yes... This is my opportunity to learn the truth. No matter how hard it is to hear... I have to know.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: I admire your courage. However, time is short. I cannot stay here for long...

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: ...Rerir had seeds of hatred in his heart, and many people nursed them for their own ends. On some level, everything he did was to try and find a way to see you again.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: But in the end, he came to regret his mistakes. He wanted to apologize for hiding his past from you...

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Beyond that... he did not say specifically what it was he wished to convey to you.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: But I'm sure that you've always been on his mind. You are what has kept him going over all these years.

dialogues.speaker: Tholindis
dialogues.text: I... I'm sorry, Miss Columbina. I just... This is so upsetting. I'm not sure how to put my feelings into words...

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: It's alright. I understand.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Well, that's everything from me. So... I guess I'll be—

dialogues.speaker: Tholindis
dialogues.text: Wait! One moment...

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Hmm?

dialogues.speaker: Tholindis
dialogues.text: Time flows backwards here. The road ahead only leads further and further into the past.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: I know. I intend to reach the end of that road.

dialogues.speaker: Tholindis
dialogues.text: Without a Moon Marrow... Without the three moons' power, you won't make it far. Wait, unless... are you... are you one of the Moon Goddesses?

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: You could say that.

dialogues.speaker: Tholindis
dialogues.text: ...I see.

dialogues.speaker: Tholindis
dialogues.text: I often think to myself... If life is like a train ride, why haven't I reached the terminus? Where am I even going?

dialogues.speaker: Tholindis
dialogues.text: And it's not just me. It's this whole place... Wherever it is, it seems like it's existed forever. It's such a mystery... Where is it going?

dialogues.speaker: Tholindis
dialogues.text: ...I must seem so ridiculous. I can't answer these basic questions, and yet I jumped right in here without hesitating... Only to be torn apart the moment I entered by powerful energy currents. Only my soul remains now.

dialogues.speaker: Tholindis
dialogues.text: Thinking back... I was suddenly overcome with fear and terror in that moment. Perhaps... I, too, became bewitched by the Abyss. I may have been the leverage it needed to control Rerir.

dialogues.speaker: Tholindis
dialogues.text: I'm... I used to be a researcher at the Universitas Magistrorum in Khaenri'ah, researching the Iridescent Moon's Marrow. Eventually, I came to the conclusion that time in here flows in reverse.

dialogues.speaker: Tholindis
dialogues.text: Rerir was one of the Vinster King's retainers. With me... he was in an impossible position. It plagued him constantly.

dialogues.speaker: Tholindis
dialogues.text: I wanted to help him escape his lot in life... I wanted him to be happy. So I thought I'd use this place to return to the past.

dialogues.speaker: Tholindis
dialogues.text: #At the time, I thought I could just go back to the day that the Vinster King first found the {M#Princess}{F#Prince}.

dialogues.speaker: Tholindis
dialogues.text: #It was only after meeting the {M#Princess}{F#Prince} that the Vinster King started going too far with his research into the Abyss. That was the day all of our woes began... I thought I could stop the king from ever meeting {M#her}{F#him}, and solve everything.

dialogues.speaker: Tholindis
dialogues.text: I couldn't kill the Vinster King himself, so I had to find another way to save Rerir. That's why I wanted to go back... to kill the person who had brought new possibilities to our realm.

dialogues.speaker: Tholindis
dialogues.text: I'm sure it was a futile endeavor, but the Abyss probably enhances the basest human desires... So I naively hoped I could change everything.

dialogues.speaker: Tholindis
dialogues.text: But I was simply too weak... Like a speck of dust against the whole universe. Look at me — I didn't even survive the journey here. Not physically, at least.

dialogues.speaker: Tholindis
dialogues.text: I know I'm never getting out of here. But you're different. You can make it, and I want to help you. I owe you that much.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: How do you plan to help me?

dialogues.speaker: Tholindis
dialogues.text: Have you noticed the golden energy that exists here?

dialogues.speaker: Tholindis
dialogues.text: Based on my past research and my observations since coming here, I believe they carry you forward faster.

dialogues.speaker: Tholindis
dialogues.text: I can share what I've learned, and help you understand the pattern in which this energy appears.

dialogues.speaker: Tholindis
dialogues.text: I think you just might... No — I know you will be able to change the past.

dialogues.speaker: Tholindis
dialogues.text: Also, I've been speculating about where this space ends.

dialogues.speaker: Tholindis
dialogues.text: The documentation was scant, but from what I know of the legends about the moons, the oldest ones seem to begin with Nibelung, king of dragonkind...

dialogues.speaker: Tholindis
dialogues.text: I have no way of verifying any of it by this point. But if it's true, you might be able to reach that era if you keep walking...

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Understood. Thank you, Miss Tholindis.

dialogues.speaker: Tholindis
dialogues.text: I'm the one who should be thanking you. If you hadn't entered this... realm of everlasting death, what use would my deductions be? Thanks to you, they have some meaning.

dialogues.speaker: Tholindis
dialogues.text: About Rerir, I... I'm so, so sorry. For everything.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: It wasn't your fault.

dialogues.speaker: Tholindis
dialogues.text: That's not true. Because we both feared bringing trouble upon each other, neither of us ever told the truth — and that dishonesty sealed our fates.

dialogues.speaker: Tholindis
dialogues.text: But enough about that. I wish you a safe journey, Miss Columbina.

dialogues.speaker: Tholindis
dialogues.text: And may the outside world never have to experience pain like this again.

dialogues.speaker: Tholindis
dialogues.text: Rerir... You're there, aren't you?

dialogues.speaker: Tholindis
dialogues.text: I cannot see you, because you exist in the future. I expect we'll be trapped in this prison of space-time for all eternity.

dialogues.speaker: Tholindis
dialogues.text: But please, gaze upon the past... and then sit for a while.

dialogues.speaker: Tholindis
dialogues.text: Let's find a place to sit down together, just like we did when we first met.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: So, you think that the moon's reflection might be where Nibelung imprisoned the Three Moon Sisters?

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: Yes. It would explain a lot, such as why that space would respond to a Moon Goddess's power, opening the Moon Gate at her command...

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: It would also explain why Miss Columbina has been unable to leave, and why time flows in reverse there...

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: In the messages she sent, Columbina promised us she'd find a way to return... But we have no way of knowing how, when, or where this might happen.

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: The fact that she still has yet to reappear in this world indicates that returning from that place is no easy feat. We cannot afford to simply wait for her.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: So you're saying... if she could return by her own power alone, she would have done so long ago.

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: Yes. She certainly wouldn't leave it to this late stage when it's so touch and go.

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: I've been giving this some thought, and I've come to believe that Luonnotar might be an "anchor" that she left behind, as a sort of future waypoint.

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: #This could also explain why Luonnotar is always by {NICKNAME}'s side.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: ...Sounds like a plausible theory. If that's the case, there must be some criteria we need to fulfill to allow Columbina to return to the present.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: The question is, what could they be?

dialogues.speaker: Dodocommunication Device
dialogues.text: Dodo! Dodoco!

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Hello? Listen up, this is extremely important!

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Sandrone frantically relays her great discovery.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Next, Nefer and Nicole present their hypothesis. As this impossible mystery finally starts to unravel, everyone starts to remember what joy feels like.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Not only is Columbina alive, but she may well exist in a form unimaginable to us.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: I'm still unclear on the details, but she's done something truly inconceivable in the past. And the clue to what she's done lies in the moon in Teyvat's sky.

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: Truly amazing. Ah, I'm so delighted for her.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: I'm sure we all feel the same. And I'm sure Columbina is ready to get back here and fight by our side.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: I'll keep my calculations going and try to find some way of coordinating with her. But that's not an excuse for everyone else to slack off, okay? All of you had better keep trying to think of solutions.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
