dialogues.text: How can the dead moons still live? And Luonnotar... hmm...

dialogues.speaker: Canon
dialogues.text: It's... hard to believe that's what will happen in the distant future...

dialogues.speaker: Aria
dialogues.text: Our authority is linked to the most fundamental rules of Teyvat... I suppose it's no wonder that many would covet that power.

dialogues.speaker: Sonnet
dialogues.text: Heh, I didn't realize that when you said "friends," you meant people who live down in Teyvat... Ah, that's so lovely. I always wanted to go down there and have some fun...

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Have you... ever tried leaving this prison?

dialogues.speaker: Sonnet
dialogues.text: Of course. Between us, we've tried everything. But no matter where we go, this space will eventually bring us back here.

dialogues.speaker: Canon
dialogues.text: It's like the center of a whirlpool. Everything ultimately converges here, at the moment when Nibelung imprisoned us.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: In that case, have you tried using any of those pathways that connect this space to the real world?

dialogues.speaker: Sonnet
dialogues.text: Sorry? What are those?

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: ...They're passages through which you can make small-scale changes to reality by using kuuvahki.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: (Or am I the only one who can use those passages? Because part of my so{RUBY#[D]Luonnotar}ul remains in reality?)

dialogues.speaker: Canon
dialogues.text: Kuuvahki...? What is that?

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: You don't know? It's... a unique kind of elemental energy found only in Nod-Krai, the land from which the moons arose.

dialogues.speaker: Canon
dialogues.text: Oh... Well, it's true that the moons first rose up from the part of Teyvat you say is called "Nod-Krai."

dialogues.speaker: Canon
dialogues.text: But there is no difference in the elemental energy between there and anywhere else.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: ...What?

dialogues.speaker: Sonnet
dialogues.text: Could you show us some of this "kuuvahki," Hyposelenia? Maybe if we see it, it'll make more sense.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Okay.

dialogues.speaker: Aria
dialogues.text: Uh... Isn't that just... your power?

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: What? ...But it's everywhere in Nod-Krai. In the air, in the land... Even the creatures who live there have adapted to its influence.

dialogues.speaker: Canon
dialogues.text: How curious... This kuuvahki certainly did not exist anywhere in the world before we were imprisoned.

dialogues.speaker: Sonnet
dialogues.text: Let alone influence living creatures. So... how exactly does it affect them, anyway? Can they float in the air like us?

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: (This is so strange... Why would their reality differ so much from mine?)

dialogues.speaker: Canon
dialogues.text: Columbina... You're looking for more than just a way out of here, aren't you?

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Yes... If I am to help my friends... I will need trilunar authority on par with that of our foe.

dialogues.speaker: Sonnet
dialogues.text: You mean... you'll need our power.

dialogues.speaker: Canon
dialogues.text: This sounds extremely risky...

dialogues.speaker: Canon
dialogues.text: The three moons' powers are not mutually compatible. Concentrating them into one goddess will be a very painful process... And if anything goes wrong, it could tear you to pieces.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: I know... but I'm willing to take that risk.

dialogues.speaker: Aria
dialogues.text: Even so... Let's say we successfully transfer our authority to you. How will you take it outside this prison?

dialogues.speaker: Aria
dialogues.text: Nibelung constructed this realm specifically to prevent us from using our powers to interfere in his war.

dialogues.speaker: Aria
dialogues.text: No moon goddess can leave this place alive...

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: What if... I don't leave alive?

dialogues.speaker: Canon
dialogues.text: Have you figured it out, Columbina?

dialogues.speaker: Canon
dialogues.text: Tell us, how do you plan to leave this place?

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: I... I intend to "die" here, in this moment, and then be reborn in the future with the help of my friends.

dialogues.speaker: Sonnet
dialogues.text: What? Wh—What are you saying? How can the dead be reborn?

dialogues.speaker: Sonnet
dialogues.text: And how will you inform these future friends of your plans? You can't exactly leave oracles — nothing can escape this place, not a single ray of moonlight...

dialogues.speaker: Sonnet
dialogues.text: And even if you found a way, what if they never find the message you've left for them? You'll... you'll...

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: No. That won't happen.

dialogues.speaker: Sonnet
dialogues.text: ...Come again?

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: They will find my message. I'm sure of it.

dialogues.speaker: Canon
dialogues.text: ...I'm not following. How exactly will you achieve this?

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: It's quite simple, really.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: First, I will leave my soul here.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: ...I see it.

dialogues.speaker: Aria
dialogues.text: Your soul? You mean, your divinity?

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Yes. I once left a portion of my soul in the future — one so small that this prison barely noticed anything.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: In this very moment, she can resonate with my soul across time.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: When the time comes, I believe that she can serve as an anchor to pull my soul from here back to the future reality...

dialogues.speaker: Canon
dialogues.text: ...Just as gravity connects the world to the moon.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Exactly. In the future, where I came from, the moon has been cast beyond the false sky, but I can still feel that it is there.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: In a similar way, I can feel a connection to the soul fragment I left behind even now. My friends can use it to detect my presence.

dialogues.speaker: Sonnet
dialogues.text: But... How do you just... leave your soul here? Is that even possible?

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: On my way here, I met an ordinary mortal who entered this place long before I did.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Her body is long gone, but her soul remains.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: And before that, I encountered an old enemy whose entire soul survives here intact, while the power that once corrupted his body has faded away.

dialogues.speaker: Canon
dialogues.text: So perhaps this space is specifically designed to imprison divi{RUBY#[D]soul}nity and authority, but not the physical body...

dialogues.speaker: Sonnet
dialogues.text: Still, even if your body can escape, would it not just be a lifeless husk without the so{RUBY#[D]divinity}ul inside?

dialogues.speaker: Sonnet
dialogues.text: Wait... Is that what you meant when you said you wouldn't leave alive...?

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Yes. I shall turn my body into moonlight, and pour it over Nod-Krai.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: That power shall protect the land and quietly blend into it, awaiting my soul's return in the future.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: However... I cannot do this on my strength alone.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: I would need your help to do this... So I'm humbly asking for your assistance.

dialogues.speaker: Aria
dialogues.text: Hah... Oh, dear sister, you need not be so formal. As I said before, we are but remnants of a bygone age.

dialogues.speaker: Aria
dialogues.text: You, on the other hand, were born alone in that distant future, and you have walked a long and lonesome road since then. How could I bear to let your story end here in this dungeon?

dialogues.speaker: Aria
dialogues.text: Don't forget — we are your sisters. Your family.

dialogues.speaker: Sonnet
dialogues.text: ...Aria's right. Actually, I always wanted a little sister. Can you imagine how it's been for me, getting nagged by two older sisters all this time?

dialogues.speaker: Sonnet
dialogues.text: Now, I finally get to be the big sis — and not just that, but I get to help you return to your world, too. How could I say no to that?

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: ...Sonnet...

dialogues.speaker: Aria
dialogues.text: Canon...?

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: ...I'm sorry. I know this is a bold request. The Frost Moon is rightfully yours, and it remains intact...

dialogues.speaker: Canon
dialogues.text: ...Oh — no, please don't misunderstand me, Columbina.

dialogues.speaker: Canon
dialogues.text: I was just... thinking back on the years that the three of us once spent together...

dialogues.speaker: Canon
dialogues.text: You cannot imagine how happy I am to hear of the future world you describe... the Frostmoon Scions, your lovely, kindly friends...

dialogues.speaker: Canon
dialogues.text: For the three of us, whose purpose in life was to maintain the peace in Teyvat, it is a great relief to know that the people of this world live in such an abundant future.

dialogues.speaker: Canon
dialogues.text: If your plan can save them and save Nod-Krai, I will gladly give you all that I can.

dialogues.speaker: Canon
dialogues.text: Besides, the three of us have been together since the day we were born. I could never abandon them to live on alone without them.

dialogues.speaker: Sonnet
dialogues.text: Canon...

dialogues.speaker: Canon
dialogues.text: Still, I do have one question I would like to ask you before we proceed.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Certainly. What is it?

dialogues.speaker: Canon
dialogues.text: Why do you cover your eyes?

dialogues.speaker: Sonnet
dialogues.text: Yeah, I was curious about that, too... but it seemed personal, so I didn't wanna intrude.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: I... There was a time when I refused to look upon the world. I believed it was full of nothing but lies and falsehoods.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: I wished to hide my feelings... seal my heart... until I could return to my true home.

dialogues.speaker: Canon
dialogues.text: I see...

dialogues.speaker: Canon
dialogues.text: Perhaps that decision saved you from ever having to see the false sky again. But at the same time, you likely missed out on many true and precious things, like the smiles on your friends' faces.

dialogues.speaker: Canon
dialogues.text: Promise me this, Columbina: When you return to the future, open your eyes, take a look at the world around you... and see your friends.

dialogues.speaker: Canon
dialogues.text: I'm sure that you know this already, given that you long to return...

dialogues.speaker: Canon
dialogues.text: But that is your true home.

dialogues.speaker: Canon
dialogues.text: Give me your hand, Columbina.

dialogues.speaker: Canon
dialogues.text: ...Aria, Sonnet, you too.

dialogues.speaker: Sonnet
dialogues.text: Okay.

dialogues.speaker: Aria
dialogues.text: Alright.

dialogues.speaker: Canon
dialogues.text: ...We once were the song sung for eternity, but now it is you who must continue to sing.

dialogues.speaker: Aria
dialogues.text: ...We once were the tides in the great river of time, but now we subside, and you arise.

dialogues.speaker: Sonnet
dialogues.text: ...We were the messengers of madness and inspiration, but now, the lies have faded, and your truth must endure.

dialogues.speaker: Canon
dialogues.text: ...We are souls awaiting the sun. You must return to be with those who smile when they see your face.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: ...It's done.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Initiate numerological array.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Continue running primary process — calculate the world's fate through extrapolation, and identify nodes of potential change.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Secondary process — scan for moons.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Still four... The number of Moon Marrows hasn't changed.

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Wait, let me think... Is it possible that there's something I've been misunderstanding about the moons all along?

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: ...Variables... Variables in the world...

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: I know where potential variables within the world come from... So, what about the moons? Are there any variables there?

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Like their life or death, for instance? What if being alive or dead makes no difference to a moon?

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: But that's so strange. Even immortal gods can die. Why would the moons alone be...

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: ...Wait. Wait! I've got it... I've got it!

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: If alive or dead is considered a variable, we might've had this wrong the whole time... No one ever said that a Moon Marrow equals a living moon. We just made that assumption ourselves!

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Initiate secondary process. Scan again, this time filtering out interfering parameter "Moon Marrow." I don't care if they're natural or artificial. Get them out of my search results!

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: ...Why? It says three moons still exist in Teyvat, even after excluding the Moon Marrows... But we know for a fact that two of them are dead!

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: Redo the scan! Narrow the results to "living moons" and "real moons"! No, scrap that — narrow it down to "moons that have lunar authority and remain alive"!

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: ...Why? Why is it still three?

dialogues.speaker: Marionette
dialogues.text: What is this, Columbina? Has the world lied to us? Or are you the one pulling the wool over our eyes?

dialogues.speaker: Columbina
dialogues.text: (...! Is that... the Rächer of Solnari?)

dialogues.speaker: Columbina
dialogues.text: (I can't believe he survived... How did he do it?)

dialogues.speaker: Columbina
dialogues.text: (He kept his word. The Abyss is no longer obstructing my path.)

dialogues.speaker: Sonnet
dialogues.text: When did you get here? How long has it been?

dialogues.speaker: Columbina
dialogues.text: I can't say for sure... But it feels like it's been forever...

dialogues.speaker: Sonnet
dialogues.text: I see... Are you feeling alright? You look a little unwell.

dialogues.speaker: Columbina
dialogues.text: I can hold out a while longer...

dialogues.speaker: Sonnet
dialogues.text: We don't have far to go. The place where my sisters and I are based is just up ahead.

dialogues.speaker: Sonnet
dialogues.text: Don't worry, they're both really nice! I'll introduce you.
